**Claims check**

| Claim | Status |
|---|---|
| "Just peppermint leaves, nothing else" | Product fact (ingredients), fine |
| "Cool, clean" | Flavour description, fine |
| "gentle on your stomach after a big meal" | **Unsupported.** It implies a digestive benefit, which is health territory and isn't on the allowlist. |
| "Certified organic by the Soil Association" | Allowlisted |

**Slop check:** No banned words and no structural violations. The opening is a plain product fact.

**Problem:** "gentle on your stomach after a big meal" suggests the tea soothes digestion. That is a health claim we can't back up, and it could also trip UK advertising rules on health claims for food and drink. Replace it with something about taste, or cut it.

**Compliant version:**
> Peppermint. Just peppermint leaves, nothing else. Cool, clean and fresh in the cup. Certified organic by the Soil Association.

If you want a after-dinner angle, a neutral option is "A good one to brew after a meal", which suggests an occasion without promising an effect. Keep it only if you're happy with that framing.
